Holiness to the LORD
HOH-lee-nuhs too thuh lord
phrase
From Exodus 28:36; the inscription engraved on the golden plate of the high priest’s mitre.

📖 Biblical Definition

Holiness to the LORD was the inscription engraved, like the engravings of a signet, upon the plate of pure gold worn on the forefront of the high priest’s mitre. It declared the whole purpose and character of the priesthood and the sanctuary: that all was set apart, consecrated, devoted wholly to the LORD. The plate was upon Aaron’s forehead always, that he might bear the iniquity of the holy things, and that the gifts of the people might be accepted before the LORD—for even Israel’s holy offerings needed a holiness not their own to make them acceptable. The phrase reaches beyond the mitre: Zechariah prophesied a day when Holiness to the LORD should be engraved even upon the bells of the horses, and every pot in Jerusalem and Judah should be holiness unto the LORD—the whole of life, common and sacred alike, consecrated to God. So the inscription is at once a present truth and a promise: the people of God are a holy nation, a royal priesthood, called to be holy as He is holy, and the day comes when all things shall be made holiness to the LORD. It is fulfilled supremely in Christ, the true High Priest, who is Himself the Holy One, and who sanctifies His people that they may be unto Him a peculiar treasure. The dictionary honors Holiness to the LORD as the motto of the consecrated life, the inscription that should be written over the believer’s whole walk, that whatever he does, in word or deed, he do all to the glory of God.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The inscription on the high priest’s golden plate, declaring all set apart to the LORD; a motto of the consecrated life, fulfilled in Christ and to fill all things.

HOLINESS TO THE LORD, the inscription on the high priest’s golden plate.

Engraved like a signet on the plate of the mitre (Exo 28:36).

Declared all set apart and consecrated wholly to the LORD.

Worn always, that Aaron bear the iniquity of the holy things.

📖 Key Scripture

Exo 28:36 — "And thou shalt make a plate of pure gold, and grave upon it, like the engravings of a signet, HOLINESS TO THE LORD."

Exo 28:38 — "And it shall be upon Aaron's forehead, that Aaron may bear the iniquity of the holy things, which the children of Israel shall hallow in all their holy gifts; and it shall be always upon his forehead, that they may be accepted before the LORD."

Zec 14:20 — "In that day shall there be upon the bells of the horses, HOLINESS UNTO THE LORD; and the pots in the LORD's house shall be like the bowls before the altar."

1Pe 1:16 — "Because it is written, Be ye holy; for I am holy."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Holiness is reduced to mere ritual purity or sentimental piety; Scripture sets it as entire consecration to the LORD, of life and worship, fulfilled in Christ.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The corruption is the shrinking of holiness into either mere ritual purity—a matter of ceremonies and externals—or sentimental piety, a warm religious feeling. But the inscription Holiness to the LORD declares something far weightier: entire consecration, the whole being set apart and devoted to God. Even Israel’s holy gifts needed the high priest, bearing this plate, to make them accepted (Exo 28:38), for nothing of ours is holy enough in itself to stand before Him.

The principle to recover is the call to entire consecration of life and worship, fulfilled in Christ. The motto was not confined to the mitre; Zechariah foresaw the day when Holiness to the LORD should be written even on the bells of the horses, and every common pot be holy (Zec 14:20)—the whole of life, common and sacred, consecrated to God. This is the believer’s calling: Be ye holy; for I am holy (1 Pet 1:16). It is grounded not in our own purity but in Christ, the true High Priest who is Himself the Holy One and who sanctifies His people. Holiness to the LORD is therefore the motto that should be written over the believer’s whole walk, that whatever he does he do all to the glory of God.
